clue.text: Second casual remark about regular type of rugby game

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second, as in time
even means regular or steady
an aside is a remark made in passing

explanation.surface: Someone passes an offhand comment about a fixture in a familiar form of rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' just joins the remark to its subject in the surface; the pieces run S, EVEN, A SIDE in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is a shortened form of rugby union played with seven players on each team rather than fifteen.

clue.text: Only one type of music on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: soul is a genre of popular music

explanation.surface: A complaint that the radio plays just one musical style.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means single or the only one, as in a sole survivor.

clue.text: Justify being very mean

parts.note: to indicate is to mean or signify

explanation.surface: A cynic asks whether stinginess can ever be defended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' reads as stingy in the surface, but it is the verb, as in signify.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate a decision is to show it was right, i.e. to justify it.

clue.text: Girl from Bognor, a hairdresser

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Bognor and into a and hairdresser

explanation.surface: Introducing a young woman who cuts hair in Bognor, a seaside town on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Norah is a female first name, and crosswords use girl to signal any woman's name.

clue.text: Cocktail is sent over — beloved cabaret's beginning inside

indicators.note: sending a word over flips it, so is is read backwards
the opening letter of cabaret goes within the word for beloved

parts.note: dear means beloved

indicators.note: only the opening letter of cabaret's is used

explanation.surface: A drink is served across the bar while a cabaret show starts.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash splits the clue into two halves; 'sent over' reads like a waiter passing a drink, but it turns the little word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a classic mixed drink of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Notice father in study, expressionless

indicators.note: the notice and father go within the word for study

parts.note: a den is a private room for work or study
an ad is an advertisement, a public notice
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Someone spots their dad reading in his study, his face blank.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face shows no emotion, so a deadpan delivery is deliberately blank.

clue.text: Primate carrying son in church recess

indicators.note: the primate holds the son within it

parts.note: an ape is a primate
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An ape carries a child into an alcove of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular vaulted recess, usually at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Earlier monastery, incomplete

indicators.note: the word for monastery loses its last letter, leaving it unfinished

parts.note: a small religious house of monks, a step below an abbey

explanation.surface: A monastery from an earlier era stands unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior means earlier or preceding, as in a prior engagement.

clue.text: Where racing takes place has mopeds staggered at the start

indicators.note: the jumbled mopeds go before the word for has
staggered means lurching about, so the letters of mopeds are jumbled

parts.note: owns means has or possesses

explanation.surface: A racecourse where riders on mopeds wobble away from the starting line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggered' suggests staggered starts on a track, but it signals a jumble, and 'has' is a verb meaning possesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is the racecourse in Surrey, England, home of the Derby horse race.

clue.text: Play causing complaint?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a comedy by Noel Coward
second meaning: an allergic ailment caused by pollen

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a play that provokes grumbling; complaint here is an illness, and the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a 1925 Coward comedy and the common term for an allergy to pollen, a minor medical complaint.

clue.text: Ship's policy read at the start

parts.note: a line is a policy or official position, as in the party line

indicators.note: only the first letter of read is taken

explanation.surface: A shipping company's rules are read aloud before departure.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship sailing a regular route.

clue.text: See 15
Close deal over a drink late on

parts.note: nigh means near or close

indicators.note: over signals that the word for deal is turned around

parts.note: a pact is a deal or agreement

explanation.surface: Two parties seal an agreement over drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is an alcoholic drink taken just before going to bed.

clue.text: Discussion group intended to reach university members, primarily

parts.note: for means aimed at, as in a gift for someone

indicators.note: only the first letter of members is used

explanation.surface: A debating society set up for members of a university.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a meeting or medium where ideas are exchanged and debated.

clue.text: Female politician, a canny sort on the rampage

indicators.note: running wild, so the letters of a canny sort are thrown about

explanation.surface: A shrewd character goes wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy Astor was the first woman to sit as an MP in the British House of Commons, in 1919.

clue.text: Community theatre perhaps traumatic, as dream shattered

indicators.note: broken into pieces, so the letters of traumatic as dream are reassembled

explanation.surface: A local stage show proves as upsetting as a broken dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateur dramatics is unpaid stage acting by local groups, of which a community theatre is one example.

clue.text: Stationery item? Penelope quietly removed about five

indicators.note: the shortened name goes around the five
the letter for quietly is taken out of Penelope

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Penelope is quietly sent away, with something about five involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' takes the first P from PENELOPE, leaving ENELOPE, and 'about' wraps that around V.
explanation.definitionFit: An envelope is a paper cover for a letter, sold among writing materials.

clue.text: Composer's new look

parts.note: novel means new or original
lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: A composer gets a fresh appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor, writer of Keep the Home Fires Burning.

clue.text: Deepest of three originally in port

parts.note: lowest means deepest

indicators.note: only the first letter of three is taken

explanation.surface: The deepest of three harbours, described from the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowestoft is a fishing town and harbour on the Suffolk coast, England's most easterly point.

clue.text: Herb, dear in Paris and centre of Seville

parts.note: cher is French for dear

indicators.note: only the central letters of Seville are kept, its outer pairs dropped

explanation.surface: A herb is praised in France and grown in the middle of a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Chervil is a delicate culinary herb related to parsley, used in French cooking.

clue.text: Student left job that makes a nice bit of money?

parts.words: job that makes a nice bit of money
parts.note: a nice little earner is British slang for a profitable job

explanation.surface: A student quits a job that paid well.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone studying a subject or skill, such as a learner driver.

clue.text: Amazingly, nephew so right not to concede defeat

indicators.note: in an astonishing way, so the letters of nephew so right not are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nephew is surprisingly correct to refuse to give in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' looks like part of the surface's refusal to give up, but it belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from boxing, where a trainer throws a sponge into the ring to surrender.

clue.text: European in danger on that account

indicators.note: European goes within the word for danger

parts.note: a threat is a danger

explanation.surface: A European finds himself at risk for that very reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereat is an archaic adverb meaning because of that, or at that point.

clue.text: Article on revolutionary investor

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: turning round, so the word for on is read backwards

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a radical who puts money into ventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel, but it reverses LEG to give GEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a backer who funds a theatrical production or a startup business.

clue.text: Visitor suspected, reportedly

indicators.note: as it is reported, i.e. by its spoken sound

parts.note: to have guessed is to have suspected

explanation.surface: A caller is said to be under suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is a person invited to stay or dine at someone's home.

clue.text: Silly mates hiding your old gemstone

indicators.note: the jumbled mates conceals the word for your old
foolish, so the letters of mates are rearranged

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: Foolish friends have stashed away an antique jewel of yours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'your old' points to the archaic form of your, which sits inside the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a violet variety of quartz prized as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Dye layer navy (first half)

parts.note: a hen is a layer, a bird that lays eggs

indicators.note: only the opening two letters of navy are used

explanation.surface: A paint or dye coat in navy blue, applied halfway.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish-brown colouring made from a plant, used on hair and skin.

clue.text: Rare new breed

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of rare are made into a fresh word

explanation.surface: An unusual new variety of animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear animals is to breed and raise them.

clue.text: See 21
Trap northern elk heading off

indicators.note: the word for elk loses its first letter

parts.note: a moose is the North American name for an elk

explanation.surface: A snare is set for an elk in the north just as it moves away.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope that tightens when pulled, used to snare animals.

clue.text: Assess offer a tender contains

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within its letters

parts.note: the letters run from the end of offer through a and into tender

explanation.surface: Judging a bid submitted in a tendering process.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to evaluate or judge its worth.

clue.text: Measuring device for farm vehicle

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A gadget for gauging something on a tractor.
explanation.definitionFit: A protractor is a semicircular instrument used to measure angles.
